one_month_reasoning: No Jabil earnings fall in the window to 2026-11-01. Q4 FY26 was reported 2026-09-30, and Q1 FY27 results (guide: $10.6-11.4B revenue, $3.80-4.20 core EPS) are due mid/late December. Events in the window: (1) the FY26 10-K, likely filed in late October, with the customer-concentration table and working-capital footnotes; this is rarely a price mover. (2) Late-October hyperscaler Q3 earnings and capex guidance, plus the Celestica and Flex prints. These are the dominant two-way swing factor for an EMS name whose FY27 guide is about 50% AI-related. (3) The late-October FOMC. The stock fell 10.0% close to close on the print (318.84 to 286.86), then retraced about 6% to 304.41. The supervisor's check shows the guide beat consensus by about 3.7% ($17.55 vs $16.92), not the 6% I had in round 1. That weakens the post-surprise drift argument, so I shrink my upward tilt from 0.52 to 0.515. Otherwise this is a near-symmetric lognormal at the usual monthly vol (47%/3.5, about 13.4%).

Compared with round 1, FY27/FY28 EPS are lower (a smaller assumed beat) and the multiple is slightly higher (Flex is at ~25x, not ~14.5x).

bear.story: AI/data-center capex digestion in 2027, or a hyperscaler program loss or insourcing. FY24 shows that Jabil's initial guide can be cut twice in a year. FY27 misses the back-end-loaded margin ramp, the Sept 2027 FY28 outlook is flat at about $17, the payables-funded working capital unwinds, and the stock de-rates to about 11.5x.

base.story: FY27 lands slightly above the $17.55 guide (~$17.80). The second hyperscaler goes above 10% of revenue and the third ramps. The Sept 2027 FY28 outlook implies about 15% EPS growth to about $20.40, valued at about 16.5x: still a deep discount to Flex at ~25x because of earnings-quality concerns.

bull.story: A repeat of the FY25/FY26 beat pattern (+13-19% vs the initial guide): FY27 about $19.5, and the FY28 outlook is about $23.5 with 6.5%+ core margin. AI revenue runs well above $22.1B, and the multiple closes part of the gap to peers, at about 20x.

thesis_break_reason: About 12.2x the FY27 guide and about 29% below today. A trade there would most likely mean the market has evidence that the $44.5B / $17.55 outlook is breaking, as it did in FY24, when the initial guide was cut twice: a guide cut at the Dec or Mar quarter, a hyperscaler program loss, AI capex retrenchment, or a working-capital unwind as $14.4B of AP normalizes. Ordinary 47% volatility took the stock from $284 to $377 over the past three months without breaking about $284, even through the post-print drop. I keep $215 rather than the supervisor's $210: it is a similar level, and with peers at ~25x, a fall to 12x would itself be a fundamental signal.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's checks changed three inputs. (1) The pre-guide consensus was $16.92, so the guide beat it by ~3.7%, not ~6%. That makes the 10% drop more of a sell-the-news move and weakens my 1-month drift tilt. (2) Flex trades at ~25x its raised FY27 guide (verified: $116.61 close, guide $4.42-4.74), not ~14.5x, so peer support for JBL's multiple is stronger than I had it. (3) The guide-beat base rate is not one-sided. I verified FY25 ($8.65 guide vs $9.75 actual) and FY24, where the initial ~$33.3B / >$9 outlook was cut in November 2023 and again in March 2024 to $28.5B / $8.40. I therefore cut my FY27 base-case beat from +3% to +1.5% ($17.80) and FY28 EPS from $20.75 to $20.40. I moved the FY26-sized beat into the bull case, as the supervisor asked. I did not find H1 bookings data; the call offers only qualitative 'committed business' and 'booked orders' language, which supports a small beat but not a large one. I raised the P/E from 16x to 16.5x on the peer evidence, but stayed far below Flex because of earnings quality (GAAP $9.75 vs core $13.09; +$8B of payables funding working capital). The net effect leaves fair value roughly unchanged at $335 (from $337), about 10% above spot. Scenarios: $195 / $335 / $470 at 25/50/25, mean about $334. The ladder is a lognormal-like distribution with median about $322 and sigma about 0.43. I trimmed the upper tail slightly from round 1 (smaller bull EPS) and fattened the left tail a little for the FY24 guide-cut precedent. The supervisor's fair value ($325) is close; my higher figure comes from the 16.5x peer-adjusted multiple, which I think is justified since JBL sits ~8 turns below Flex. Research limits: the FY26 10-K is not yet filed, so customer concentration still comes from the Q3 10-Q.
